title: The skeleton dog and the tennis ball
summary: One start picture and one detailed prompt bring a playful skeleton dog to life.

scenes.prompt:
3D Pixar-style cartoon animation, bright friendly colors, expressive characters. Maintain the exact art style, characters, lighting and layout of the starting frame.

Create ONE continuous 15-second cinematic vertical video based on the reference image.

The skeleton dog is the only main character. Preserve the exact same skeleton dog throughout: identical skull, skeletal anatomy, body proportions, blue collar, round paw tag and playful personality. Keep the same bright sunny suburban backyard.

0–2 seconds — INSTANT HOOK:
Start with an extreme close-up of a human HAND holding a bright green tennis ball near the camera. Do NOT show the person's face or full body. Behind the ball, the skeleton dog is already extremely excited—bouncing on its front paws, staring intensely at the ball, jaw open happily and vertebral tail rattling rapidly.

Off-camera voice: “Ready?”

The hand quickly pulls backward and throws the tennis ball.

2–5 seconds — CHASE:
Follow the green tennis ball with a fast cinematic whip-pan. The skeleton dog instantly explodes into a sprint after it.

Transition smoothly into a very low ground-level tracking shot alongside the running skeleton dog. Its four skeletal legs move naturally like a real running dog. Grass kicks up beneath its paws. The green tennis ball remains clearly visible ahead.

Off-camera voice: “GO!”

5–8 seconds — WOW / COMEDY MOMENT:
The tennis ball bounces once.

Skeleton dog makes a dramatic leap toward it.

While airborne, ONE single long lower-leg bone from ONE rear leg accidentally pops cleanly loose with a funny harmless POP!

Brief cinematic slow motion.

Clearly show TWO objects flying through the same frame:

1. Bright GREEN tennis ball
2. ONE WHITE dog bone

The dog notices the flying bone and looks surprised.

No pain. No injury. Pure physical comedy.

The tennis ball lands and rolls to the LEFT.

The detached bone lands and bounces to the RIGHT.

8–11 seconds — THE CHOICE:
Dog lands safely and immediately stops between the two objects.

Camera moves closer to the dog's skull.

Dog looks LEFT at the tennis ball.

Then RIGHT at its bone.

LEFT again.

RIGHT again.

Cute confused head tilt.

Music completely stops for a brief comedic pause.

11–15 seconds — PAYOFF:
Dog suddenly makes its decision.

It completely IGNORES THE TENNIS BALL.

It excitedly hops a short distance toward its detached bone, grabs its own bone horizontally in its mouth, turns around and proudly runs/hops directly toward the camera.

Keep the abandoned green tennis ball clearly visible behind the dog for a moment so viewers instantly understand the joke.

Off-camera owner laughs:

“That's YOUR bone!”

Dog approaches very close to camera proudly carrying its own bone, skeletal tail wagging wildly.

Finish with the happy skeleton dog's skull filling the frame, bone held in its mouth.

HARD CUT.

CAMERA: extreme close-up hook → whip-pan with ball → low tracking chase → brief slow-motion leap → clear wide ball-vs-bone composition → skull reaction close-up → backward tracking payoff.

AUDIO: playful energetic music, excited bark, bone-tail clattering, ball whoosh, fast skeletal footsteps, clear comedic POP, bone clink-clink, tennis-ball bounce, sudden silence during the choice, happy bark and owner laughter at the end.

STRICT CONTINUITY: Same skeleton dog for the entire video. Same skull, collar, tag, bone proportions and size. Dog begins with exactly four legs. Only ONE rear-leg bone detaches. Only ONE loose bone exists. The missing bone must remain missing while the dog carries it.

DO NOT show a human face or full human character. Human presence is limited to the hand/forearm throwing the ball and the off-camera voice.

No fur, skin, flesh, muscles, organs, blood, wounds, pain, horror, costume, transformation, extra legs, duplicated bones, duplicated balls or duplicated dogs.

Narration voice: a warm, sunny female narrator.

Playful, upbeat background music.

No text overlays, no logos, no watermarks.
